skill.name: code-review
skill.description: Perform code reviews following Sentry engineering practices. Use when reviewing pull requests, examining code changes, or providing feedback on code quality. Covers security, performance, testing, and design review.
skill.summary: Review code for correctness, security, performance, design quality, and test coverage using Sentry engineering practices.
skill.author: davila7

content.user_title: Review Code with Sentry Engineering Practices
content.value_statement: Pull requests can hide defects, security gaps, performance regressions, and weak tests. This skill applies a structured Sentry-inspired checklist and produces prioritized, actionable review feedback.
actual_capabilities: Checks changes for runtime errors, performance regressions, side effects, compatibility issues, ORM inefficiencies, and security vulnerabilities.
Assesses architecture fit, component interactions, and alignment with project requirements.
Evaluates functional, integration, and end-to-end test coverage for requirements and edge cases.
Flags schema, API, framework, performance, and security changes that need senior review.
Produces polite, actionable feedback and distinguishes blocking issues from minor style concerns.
Recognizes common Python, Django, TypeScript, React, and SQL review patterns.
limitations: Provides guidance from supplied context and does not execute tests or verify runtime behavior.
Uses general Sentry practices; repository-specific standards still require project documentation.
Example coverage is strongest for Python, Django, TypeScript, React, and SQL.
Cannot confirm production impact without relevant code, tests, requirements, and architecture context.

use_cases.title: Pull Request Review
use_cases.description: Review a feature branch for correctness, security, performance, design, and test coverage before approval.

use_cases.title: Architecture Risk Triage
use_cases.description: Identify changes needing deeper review, including schema, API, framework, performance-critical, and security-sensitive work.

use_cases.title: Review Quality Coaching
use_cases.description: Help reviewers write specific, empathetic feedback and avoid blocking changes for personal style preferences.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Change Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the following code change. Identify correctness issues, security risks, performance concerns, and missing tests. Prioritize findings by impact: {{change}}
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for a focused review of a small change.

prompt_templates.title: Pull Request Assessment
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this pull request against its requirements. Check design fit, side effects, backward compatibility, test coverage, and actionable feedback: {{requirements}} {{diff}}
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when requirements and the complete change are available.

prompt_templates.title: Framework-Specific Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this {{language_or_framework}} change. Examine framework patterns, query behavior, state management, security, edge cases, and test quality: {{diff}}
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for Python, Django, TypeScript, React, or similar framework changes.

prompt_templates.title: High-Risk Change Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this high-risk change with architecture and migration context. Identify blocking defects, rollout risks, observability gaps, and areas needing senior review: {{context}} {{diff}}
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for schema, API, framework, performance-critical, or security-sensitive changes.

output_examples.input: Review a Django endpoint that loads each related profile inside a loop.
output: High: This access pattern may issue one profile query per user. Prefetch profiles before iteration and add a query-count regression test.
Testing: Cover empty results and larger collections to verify correctness and bounded query growth.

output_examples.input: Review a React effect that uses a changing user identifier but declares no dependencies.
output: Medium: The effect can use a stale identifier. Include the identifier in the dependency list.
Testing: Verify that changing users refreshes the displayed data without retaining the previous response.

output_examples.input: Review a database lookup that inserts a request parameter directly into SQL text.
output: High: Direct insertion of request data creates SQL injection risk. Use parameter binding.
Testing: Add hostile input cases and confirm the database treats the value only as data.

best_practices: Provide the change, requirements, tests, and relevant architecture context.
Ask for findings ordered by severity with file and line references when available.
Validate important findings with tests, profiling, or domain experts before merging.
anti_patterns: Do not request approval from a description without the actual change.
Do not treat style preferences as blocking defects unless project standards require them.
Do not accept suggested fixes without checking repository conventions and behavior.

faq.question: What code can this skill review?
faq.answer: It can review supplied changes in any language, with specific examples for Python, Django, TypeScript, React, and SQL.

faq.question: Does the skill execute code or tests?
faq.answer: No. It reviews provided context and recommends checks, but it does not prove runtime behavior.

faq.question: Can it approve a pull request?
faq.answer: It can recommend approval or changes. A responsible maintainer should make the final decision.

faq.question: Does it review security concerns?
faq.answer: Yes. It checks for injection, cross-site scripting, access control gaps, secret exposure, and other visible risks.

faq.question: Is it limited to Sentry repositories?
faq.answer: No. The checklist is broadly useful, but each repository should supply its own standards and architecture context.

faq.question: What context produces the best review?
faq.answer: Provide the diff, requirements, tests, repository conventions, and relevant architecture or migration details.
